podcast.title: First Concert: Queen (1982)
podcast.body: At the age of 10 in 1982, Taylor Hawkins attended his first concert, which was Queen. This experience profoundly impacted him, sparking his lifelong obsession with rock and roll and his dream of being in a huge rock band. "In 1982, when he was 10, he attended his first concert. And that was Queen."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Beat-Up 1986 Toyota 4x4 Pickup Truck
podcast.body: Taylor Hawkins drove a beat-up 1986 Toyota 4x4 pickup truck, which he had bought for $400 in high school. This choice of vehicle, alongside his 2005 Subaru Baja, highlighted his down-to-earth personality and lack of concern for flashy rock star possessions. "He was driving the same beat up 1986 Toyota 4x4 pickup truck that he bought for $400 when he was in high school."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Joining Sass Jordan's Backup Band (1994)
podcast.body: In 1994, Taylor Hawkins secured a gig in the backup band for Canadian singer Sass Jordan after meeting someone at a music store who connected him. This opportunity allowed him to go on tour to Europe, marking his first experience in a rock and roll touring band. "Eventually he got a gig in the backup band for Canadian singer, Sass Jordan."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Drummer for Alanis Morissette (1995)
podcast.body: After Alanis Morissette's "Jagged Little Pill" album blew up in 1995, Taylor Hawkins became her drummer at age 23 for her "Can't Not" tour. He appeared in several of her music videos and performed with her during her debut on David Letterman in 1995. "That Sass Jordan job morphed into a gig with Alannis Morissette."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: 2001 Heroin Overdose and Coma
podcast.body: In 2001, not long after joining the Foo Fighters, Taylor Hawkins developed a serious heroin problem. While he partied extensively, he denied being a junkie until an incident in London where he took "the wrong line with the wrong thing," leading to an overdose. This overdose put him in a coma for two weeks, an event he ironically referred to as his "happy nap." "That OD put Taylor in a coma that lasted two weeks. He calls it his happy nap."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Heroin Overdose and Coma (2001)
podcast.body: In 2001, Taylor Hawkins experienced a heroin overdose at a party in London, which resulted in a two-week coma. Dave Grohl stayed by his side throughout this period, and Taylor later stated that the incident "scared him straight" regarding drug use, although he never elaborated on his sobriety. "He ingested some heroin at a party in London back in 2001 and landed in a coma for two weeks."

podcast.title: Taylor Hawkins and the Co-Tale Riders (2006)
podcast.body: In 2006, Taylor Hawkins formed his own band, Taylor Hawkins and the Co-Tale Riders, a name reflecting his sense of humor and humbleness. The band featured crack session musicians and released three albums, collaborating with figures like Roger Taylor and Brian May (Queen), Nancy Wilson (Heart), Joe Walsh (Eagles), Chrissie Hynde (Pretenders), and LeAnn Rimes. "The first came in 2006 when he formed a band called Taylor Hawkins and the Co-Tale Riders."

podcast.body: Taylor Hawkins participated in SOS All Stars, a special one-off drummers' group formed for the Live Earth show in London in 2007. He was joined by Roger Taylor of Queen and Chad Smith of the Red Hot Chili Peppers, showcasing his connections within the drumming community. "In addition to the Coat Tale writers, there was SOS All Stars."

podcast.title: The Birds of Satan (2014) - Prog Rock Side Project
podcast.body: In 2014, Taylor Hawkins formed another side project called The Birds of Satan, a band with a strong prog rock sound. The group introduced itself with a 10-minute epic song titled "The Ballad of the Birds of Satan" and featured appearances from Dave Grohl, Pat Smear, and Foo Fighters keyboardist Rami Jaffee. "In 2014, he formed a side project called The Birds of Satan, a very prog rock band that introduced itself with a 10-minute epic song entitled The Ballad of the Birds of Satan."

podcast.title: December 2021 Health Scare
podcast.body: On December 9, 2021, the Foo Fighters' private jet was bound for Chicago to connect to a flight for Abu Dhabi, where they were scheduled to play the Formula One race season finale. However, a band member, believed to be Taylor Hawkins, had to be rushed to the hospital upon landing in Chicago, allegedly due to exhaustion and dehydration, which was unconfirmed by the band. This incident caused the band to miss their Abu Dhabi connection. "When the private jet landed in Chicago, a member of the band had to be rushed to hospital. We know this to be true, and that member seems to have been tailor."

podcast.title: Death (March 25, 2022)
podcast.body: Taylor Hawkins died on Friday, March 25, 2022, in Bogotá, Colombia, at the Four Seasons Casa Medina. An ambulance was called after reports of severe chest pains, but a private doctor could not help, and he was already gone by the time EMS arrived. "Taylor left us. The Fouce fighters were touring South America, and were about to perform at the Estarial picnic in Boca-Tac, Colombia on Friday March 25th, 2022."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Final Tour Stop and Hotel Stay (March 2022)
podcast.body: In March 2022, while on a post-pandemic tour of South America, the Foo Fighters checked into the Four Seasons Casa Medina Hotel in Bogota, Colombia, on Friday, March 25, ahead of their scheduled performance. Taylor Hawkins was reportedly tired, which was not unusual for a touring musician, possibly exacerbated by Bogota's high altitude (over 2600 meters or 8,000 feet) and thin air. "On Friday the 25th of March, the band was scheduled to play in Bogota, Colombia, and had checked into the four seasons Casamadena Hotel in the city's Chapanero district."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: NHC (2022) - Most Recent Project
podcast.body: Taylor Hawkins' most recent musical project was NHC, where 'H' stood for Hawkins. The 'N' was Dave Navarro and the 'C' was Chris Cheney, both from Jane's Addiction. Taylor described the band's sound as landing "somewhere between Rush and the Faces," and they released the song "Feed the Cruel" in early 2022. "His most recent project was called NHC."

podcast.title: Beginnings as a Drummer
podcast.body: Taylor Hawkins started playing drums in 1982, the same year he attended his first Queen concert. He consistently credited his mother for her encouragement, which fostered his ambition to dream big in his musical pursuits. "That was the year he also started playing drums."

podcast.title: Cardiac Arrest and Unclear Details of Death
podcast.body: Around 7:40 PM on March 25, 2022, before the Foo Fighters were scheduled to play the Festival Estéreo Picnic, details become murky. Some reports indicate Taylor Hawkins began experiencing chest pains, while others state he was found unconscious after repeated knocking on his hotel room door. Medical personnel arrived within minutes, administered CPR, but it was too late; he suffered cardiac arrest and died. "Whatever the case, medical personnel arrived within a few minutes. CPR was administered, but it was too late. Taylor suffered cardiac arrest and died."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Conspiracy Theories and Unknown Cause of Heart Attack
podcast.body: Despite his known heart condition, conspiracy theorists speculated that his cardiomyopathy might be linked to a COVID vaccine. The ultimate cause of what made his heart stop, leading to cardiac arrest, remains officially unknown, with no public report or announcement from the Foo Fighters or other authorities. "What killed Taylor Hawkins? We may never know."

podcast.title: Distaste for Rock Star Trappings
podcast.body: Taylor Hawkins expressed a personal indifference to the stereotypical trappings of rock stardom. He prioritized playing music for the love of it rather than for wealth or fame, maintaining a grounded perspective despite his success. "If you want to play music, play because you want to play music, not because you want to be rich and famous."

podcast.title: Drumming Influences
podcast.body: Taylor Hawkins' drumming style was heavily influenced by progressive rock drummers such as Neil Peart of Rush, Stewart Copeland of The Police, and Phil Collins during his time with Genesis. Other influences included Stephen Perkins of Jane's Addiction, Ringo Starr, and his hero, Roger Taylor of Queen. "His heroes were Neil Pirate of Rush, Stuart Copeland of the police, and Phil Collins when he was with Genesis."

podcast.title: Early Life and Move to California
podcast.body: Taylor Hawkins was born in Fort Worth, Texas, on February 17, 1972. His family relocated to California when he was approximately four years old, shaping his upbringing in Orange County. "He's a Texas boy born in Fort Worth on February 17th, 1972."

podcast.title: Enlarged Heart
podcast.body: The early report following Taylor Hawkins' death stated that his heart was enlarged, weighing 600 grams, which is twice the normal size for a person of his age and size. An enlarged heart is a symptom of various underlying conditions and, if untreated, can lead to serious cardiac issues including sudden cardiac arrest. "The early report also said that Taylor's heart was enlarged."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Enlarged Heart Condition
podcast.body: Taylor Hawkins had an enlarged heart, known as a "runner's heart," a condition common in individuals who push their bodies physically for many years. This was consistent with Hawkins' physically demanding lifestyle, including three-hour Foo Fighters shows, BMX biking, and surfing. His doctor was aware of the condition and reportedly not overly concerned. "We do know that Taylor had an enlarged heart, a so-called runner's heart. And that happens when you push your body physically for years and years."

podcast.title: Influence of Jane's Addiction
podcast.body: Taylor Hawkins cited Jane's Addiction as a major influence that changed his musical direction in high school. Prior to hearing them, he listened to older classic rock and new wave, but Jane's Addiction's raw, "disgusting," and "awesome" style resonated with him, inspiring him to be like them. "And then when I heard Jane's addiction, because I was really... It was all warrant and all that kind of crap, you know."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Jane's Addiction as Personal "Punk Rock"
podcast.body: Taylor Hawkins was disillusioned with the "blah music" of hair metal (like Warrant) during his high school years. Hearing Jane's Addiction was a transformative experience, as he found them "disgusting," "awesome," and "scary," providing a raw energy that resonated with him much like punk rock did for others. "And then I heard Jane's addiction and it was like, dude, I could play like the dudes in the poster. But they were a mess and they were disgusting and they were awesome and they were scary."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Joy and Gratitude for His Career
podcast.body: Taylor Hawkins consistently conveyed immense joy and gratitude for his profession, feeling incredibly lucky to "get paid tons of money to go play rock and roll." He viewed his life as awesome, emphasizing the simple, pure enjoyment of what he did for a living. "Now we're really lucky."

podcast.title: Last Voicemail to Perry Farrell
podcast.body: At some point before his death, Taylor Hawkins left a voicemail for his friend Perry Farrell, saying, "take care of each other, and I'll take care of myself. And I'll see you in São Paulo. I love, love, love you. Sleep well." These words are considered to be potentially his final communication. "He said, take care of each other, and I'll take care of myself. And I'll see you in São Paulo. I love, love, love you. Sleep well."

podcast.title: Toxicology Report Findings
podcast.body: A preliminary toxicology report after Taylor Hawkins' death indicated the presence of 10 different substances in his system, including weed, opioids, and antidepressants. While many of these could have been prescription medicines, the report also noted an enlarged heart. "A preliminary toxicology report said that there were 10 different substances in Taylor's system, ranging from weed and opioids to antidepressants."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Unreleased Autopsy Results and Toxicology Findings
podcast.body: The official autopsy results for Taylor Hawkins have never been made public. A urine test conducted immediately after his death revealed traces of opioids, sedatives, antidepressants, and THC. While some quickly attributed these findings to his cause of death, a urine test is not as precise as a blood test for toxicology, and the specific type of opioids (potentially routine painkillers like codeine for a hard-hitting drummer in his 50s) or the concentration of other substances remain unknown. THC can also linger in the bloodstream for up to a month. "A urine test taken immediately following his death revealed traces of opioids, sedatives, and sea depressants, and some THC."

xref.title: Taylor Hawkins' Death (March 25, 2022)
xref.body: Foo Fighters drummer Taylor Hawkins died suddenly on March 25, 2022, in Bogota, Colombia, just before the band was set to headline a festival. At approximately 7:40 PM on that Friday night, a call was made from a Four Seasons property reporting a guest with severe chest pains, but EMS responders arrived too late. Officially, he died from complications related to an enlarged heart (cardiomegaly), which weighed 600 grams (compared to a normal 300 grams). Although his doctors were aware of his enlarged heart for years, attributing it to his active lifestyle of surfing, biking, and intense drumming, little other information regarding his death was released, due to an "airtight" news blackout imposed by the band and management. This lack of information fueled conspiracy theories, though sources suggested a congenital problem exacerbated by exhaustion, as Hawkins had reportedly been feeling "rough" in the months leading up to the South American tour. His death profoundly impacted Dave Grohl, the Foo Fighters, and millions of fans globally. "Taylor was dead. Officially, he died of complications involving an enlarged heart, something called cardiomagalley."

xref.body: Dave Grohl's grief over Taylor Hawkins' death is compared to his experience with Kurt Cobain's death, noting that his bond with Taylor was much deeper. While Kurt was "just a guy in his band," Taylor was his best friend. "It's shades of Kurt all over again."

xref.title: Dave Grohl's Concern for Taylor Hawkins

xref.title: Limited Musical Knowledge Focused on Hardcore
xref.body: Nate Mendel admits to having the "least depth of musical knowledge" among his bandmates, primarily caring about hardcore music for a formative period of about ten years. He often relies on Taylor Hawkins to introduce him to other bands, such as Boston. "I only cared about hardcore for about 10 years. Like those formative 10 years."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Live Performance Description
xref.body: Taylor Hawkins recounted seeing Jane's Addiction perform "seven nights up here in LA" at the John Anson Ford Theater. He was struck by the intensity of their live show, recalling a moment when a "fairy fairy" with green dreadlocks came on stage and immediately confronted a front-row audience member. "I mean, I went to John Hansen for a theater. They did seven nights up here in LA and I was just like, a, a, a fairy fairy came out on stage with green dreadlocks and a woman's hat on and told the first guy in the front row to the second he came out on stage. I was like, these guys are crazy."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Member of SOS All Stars
xref.body: Roger Taylor joined Taylor Hawkins and Chad Smith in the one-off drummers' group SOS All Stars for the Live Earth show in London in 2007. This performance brought together influential drummers for a special event. "He was joined by Roger Taylor, of course, and Chad Smith of the Red Hot Chili Peppers."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Nancy Wilson Collaboration
xref.body: Nancy Wilson of Heart was among the notable musicians who joined Taylor Hawkins on his Co-Tale Riders albums. Her contribution added to the project's broad musical scope and impressive roster of guest artists. "So did Nancy Wilson of Heart."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Near Dissolution After Taylor Hawkins's Overdose
xref.body: The Foo Fighters nearly disbanded after drummer Taylor Hawkins's severe heroin overdose in London in 2001, which put him in a two-week coma. Frontman Dave Grohl was unwilling to endure another situation where a band member might die, leading to uncertainty about the band's future and a temporary hiatus for Grohl. "But it was anything but in fact that was almost the end of the Foo Fighters. Dave Groha had no intention of going through another situation where a band may die."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Past Heroin Overdose in London
xref.body: Taylor Hawkins had previously overdosed on heroin 20 years earlier at a party in London, which resulted in a two-week coma. "He OD'd on heroin 20 years earlier at a party in London. It was in a coma for two weeks."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: In Memoriam of Those Lost in 2022

xref.title: Perry Farrell's Stage Presence
xref.body: Taylor Hawkins recounted witnessing Jane's Addiction's Perry Farrell performing with green dreadlocks and a woman's hat during their "seven nights up here in LA." Farrell's audacious and "crazy" stage persona deeply impressed Hawkins, who considered them "the best at that time." "Perry Farrell came out on stage with green dreadlocks. Woman's hat on and told the first guy in the front row to... The second he came out on stage, and I was like, these guys are crazy."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Phil Collins as Drumming Hero
xref.body: Phil Collins, particularly during his time with Genesis, was one of Taylor Hawkins' drumming heroes. Collins' influential style in the progressive rock genre contributed to Hawkins' own musical development. "and Phil Collins when he was with Genesis."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Post-Nirvana Feud with Courtney Love
xref.body: A significant feud developed between Dave Grohl and Courtney Love after Kurt Cobain's death. The first public evidence of bad blood was a 1999 interview where Dave Grohl, when asked for his favorite Hole song, replied "Teenage Horror" because it was "the one I know Courtney actually wrote," implying she didn't write others. Courtney Love subsequently attacked Dave in the media over legal disputes concerning Nirvana's music, accusing him of being sexually obsessed with Kurt Cobain and claiming he hired Taylor Hawkins as Foo Fighters' drummer because of Hawkins' resemblance to Kurt. "The first evidence I can find of some kind of bad blood was an interview Dave gave in 1999, a few years after the food fighters got going."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Precedent for Band Disbanding After Drummer's Death
xref.body: Led Zeppelin's decision to disband after John Bonham's death on September 25, 1980, serves as a significant precedent for the Foo Fighters' situation after Taylor Hawkins' passing. The band determined that "without Bonzo, there was no Led Zeppelin," and consequently folded. "When John Bonham died on September 25, 1980, there was no question that the band was done."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Production/Engineering Credits
xref.body: Sylvia Massy worked behind the board for a wide array of prominent artists, including Aerosmith, Prince, Bobby Brown, the Red Hot Chili Peppers, Slayer, Tom Petty and the Heartbreakers, Katting Kage, Johnny Cash, a Taylor Hawkins and Civil Project, System of a Down, The Smashing Pumpkins, The Black Crowes, and The Beastie Boys. This extensive list showcases her versatility and expertise across genres. "Since then, she's worked behind the board for Erasmith, Prince, Bobby Brown, the Red Hot Chili Peppers Slayer, Tom Petty and the Heartbreakers Catering Cache, Johnny Cash, a Taylor Hawkins and Civil Project, System of a Down, The Smashing Pumpkins, The Black Cros and The Beastie Boys."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Profound Influence on Taylor Hawkins
xref.body: Jane's Addiction significantly impacted Taylor Hawkins in high school, reshaping his musical tastes from older classic rock and new wave to a more alternative sound. He considered them his "punk rock" and became a complete "disciple" of the band, admiring their raw, "disgusting," "awesome," and "scary" aesthetic. "And then I heard Jane's addiction. And then it was like, dude, I could play like dudes in the poster."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Proposed Cause of Death: Cardiac Episode
xref.body: In the opinion of the speaker, Taylor Hawkins died of a cardiac episode brought on by a previously diagnosed enlarged heart, which doctors were aware of but not concerned about, attributing it to years of intense drumming, mountain biking, and surfing, dubbing it a "runner's heart." "And in my opinion, he died of some kind of cardiac episode brought on by a previously diagnosed enlarged heart. A doctor knew all about it, but he wasn't worried, saying that all that heart muscle was the result of many years of intense drumming, plus mountain biking and surfing. They called this a runner's heart."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: In Memoriam of Those Lost in 2022

xref.title: Stephen Perkins as Drumming Influence
xref.body: Stephen Perkins, the drummer for Jane's Addiction, was acknowledged as a "great drummer" and a significant influence on Taylor Hawkins. Perkins' drumming style was a key component of Jane's Addiction's appeal to Hawkins. "Other influences include Stephen Perkins of Jane's Diction, Great Drummer."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Stewart Copeland as Drumming Hero
xref.body: Stewart Copeland, the drummer for The Police, was one of Taylor Hawkins' drumming heroes. Copeland's style was a significant influence on Hawkins' own technique and approach to the instrument. "Stewart Copeland of the police."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Taylor Hawkins as Drummer for "Can't Not" Tour
xref.body: After the massive success of "Jagged Little Pill" in 1995, Taylor Hawkins, then 23, became Alanis Morissette's drummer for her "Can't Not" tour. He also appeared in several of her music videos and performed with her on her debut appearance on David Letterman. "If you saw her can't not tour, Taylor was the drummer."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Taylor Hawkins as the "Most Important" Member After Dave Grohl
xref.body: Taylor Hawkins was considered by many, next to Dave Grohl, to be the most important member of the Foo Fighters, a beloved fan favorite. Despite Dave Grohl being the chief songwriter and frontman, Taylor was allowed to "steal the show" and was a crucial personality within the group. "And next to Dave, Taylor was, I dare say, the most important, a fan favorite, beloved by fans."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Taylor Hawkins' All-Time Favorite Band
xref.body: Queen held a special place as Taylor Hawkins' all-time favorite band. He greatly admired their music and often dared to tackle Freddie Mercury's vocal parts when he would step out from behind the drum kit to sing for the Foo Fighters. "Queen was his all time favorite band."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Taylor Hawkins' Collaboration and Touring
xref.body: Taylor Hawkins performed on an album by Coheed and Cambria and also toured with them for a period. This highlights his willingness to collaborate with and support other bands outside of his main projects. "He performed on a co-heating Cambria album and even toured with them a bit."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Taylor Hawkins' Death in Bogota
xref.body: Foo Fighters drummer Taylor Hawkins experienced some kind of distress in a hotel room in Bogota, Colombia, just hours before the band was scheduled to play a festival, and died despite a doctor being called. "Fufaiter's drummer Taylor Hawkins. He went into some kind of distress in a hotel room in Bogota, Colombia. Hours before the band was supposed to play a festival. The doctor was called, but it was too late and he died."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: In Memoriam of Those Lost in 2022

xref.title: Taylor Hawkins' Favorite Drummer Ever
xref.body: Roger Taylor was Taylor Hawkins' favorite drummer of all time. This admiration was evident from Hawkins' enthusiastic reaction to a poster of Taylor's solo album "Fun in Space" at the Foo Fighters' studio. "That's Roger Taylor, man. He's my favorite drummer ever."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Taylor Hawkins' First Concert
xref.body: Queen was Taylor Hawkins' first concert experience in 1982 when he was 10 years old. This event was a turning point for him, initiating his "obsession with rock and roll" and his desire to be in a huge rock band. "Queen was my first concert and I've always been a fan."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Taylor Hawkins' First Group
xref.body: Sylvia was Taylor Hawkins' very first musical group, based in Orange County, California. This band was formed in an area where reggae music was popular, and hard rock was generally "frowned upon." "His first group was in Orange County, if it called Sylvia."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Taylor Hawkins' First Rock and Roll Gig
xref.body: Canadian singer Sass Jordan gave Taylor Hawkins his first "rock and roll check" (paycheck) when he joined her backup band in 1994. Hawkins toured Europe with her, opening for an aerospace band, which was his initial taste of being in a touring rock band. "She gave me my first rock and roll chick. And check... Not chick, check..."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Taylor Hawkins' Guest Drumming
xref.body: Taylor Hawkins contributed his drumming talents to records by Slash. This is an example of his extensive session work and collaborations with other prominent rock musicians. "He also showed up in records by Slash, Ozzy Osborne, and Elton John."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Taylor Hawkins' Guest Drumming
xref.body: Taylor Hawkins performed drums on records by Ozzy Osborne. This collaboration highlights his versatility and the respect he garnered within the rock community. "He also showed up in records by Slash, Ozzy Osborne, and Elton John."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Taylor Hawkins' Guest Drumming
xref.body: Taylor Hawkins contributed drums to records by Elton John. This collaboration demonstrates Hawkins' diverse musical engagements beyond his primary bands. "He also showed up in records by Slash, Ozzy Osborne, and Elton John."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Taylor Hawkins' Lead Vocals
xref.body: Taylor Hawkins was the only member other than Dave Grohl to sing lead on Foo Fighters songs. He sang on covers like Pink Floyd's "Have a Cigar" (with Brian May on guitar), Cream's "I Feel Fine," and Joe Walsh's "Life of Illusion," as well as original songs like "Cold Day in the Sun" and "Sunday Rain." "Just to show you how special a place Taylor Hawkins had within the food fighters, he is the only guy other than Dave Grohl to sing lead on a food song."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Taylor Hawkins' Overdose Scare (Early 2000s)
xref.body: Two decades prior to his death in 2022, Foo Fighters drummer Taylor Hawkins experienced a major health scare involving a heroin overdose, which resulted in a critical two-week coma. This incident reportedly led to a significant change in his lifestyle, as he subsequently abstained from drugs and engaged in extensive physical activity. "Two decades earlier, Taylor had a big scare when he overdosed on heroin and ended up in a touch and go coma for about two weeks."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 100 Greatest Rock Moments of the Millennium So Far - Part 6: (50-41)

xref.title: Taylor Hawkins' Unique Drumming Style
xref.body: Taylor Hawkins brought a distinct drumming style to the Foo Fighters, influenced by prog rock. His approach was subtly different and gave the band an "extra" dimension compared to other drummers like Dave Grohl, who was known for a hard-hitting style akin to John Bonham. "Taylor could play just as hard, but his style brought in a few prog rock influences, something that gave the foods something extra."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Temporary Departure and QOTSA Drumming
xref.body: After Taylor Hawkins's near-fatal overdose in 2001, Dave Grohl stepped away from the Foo Fighters to "sort his head out." During this period, he briefly became the drummer for Queens of the Stone Age. "That's when he briefly became drummer for Queens of the Stone Age."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Tribute After Death
xref.body: Ozzy Osborne was among the many musicians who sent tributes upon Taylor Hawkins' death, underscoring the widespread respect and admiration he commanded from his peers. "When he died, tributes came in from everyone from Ozzy Osborne to Stevie Nicks, to Travis Barker, to Tom Morello to Liam Gallagher."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Uncertain Future Post-Taylor Hawkins' Death
xref.body: The Foo Fighters face an uncertain future following the death of Taylor Hawkins, who was considered irreplaceable due to his chemistry and friendship with Dave Grohl and his essential role in the band's "family nature." Comparisons are drawn to Led Zeppelin, which disbanded after John Bonham's death, and Rush, which retired after Neil Peart's death. "What do the Fufighters do now? We don't know."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Unexplained Incident Preceding Death
xref.body: Three and a half months after the unexplained medical emergency in December 2021 that caused a gig cancellation, Taylor Hawkins died, leaving the exact circumstances unknown. "There was never any explanation of what happened, but it was bad enough for the band to cancel the gig. And then three and a half months later, Taylor was gone. Why? How? We may never know."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: In Memoriam of Those Lost in 2022

xref.title: Urine Test Findings and OD Dismissal
xref.body: A urine test after Taylor Hawkins's death revealed traces of opioids, antidepressants, anti-anxiety medications, and THC, but the speaker dismisses the theory of an overdose due to the nature of a urine test (not blood), unknown concentrations/combinations, and potential for common substances like codeine in cough syrup or lingering THC. "There were those who will say the drugs were involved in his death, but frankly, I don't believe it. And yes, a urine test after he died revealed traces of opioids and he depressants anti-anxiety medications in THC. But that was a urine test, not a blood test. And we don't know the exact concentrations or combinations of those drugs. So to say that he died from an OD is jumping to conclusions."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: In Memoriam of Those Lost in 2022

xref.title: William Goldsmith's Departure
xref.body: Drummer William Goldsmith was replaced by Taylor Hawkins after difficulties during the recording sessions for "The Colour and the Shape" album. Dave Grohl was reportedly unhappy with Goldsmith's performance and re-recorded all his drum parts, prompting the change. "Dave even went in and re-recorded all of Goldsmith's parts."
